title: On Covering the wall with old newspapers
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：cover　|　正文 349 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cover 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the operator ① covered the wall with old newspapers on the same day, and every trainee in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the operator ② covers the wall with old newspapers before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ cover the wall with old newspapers at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ covered the wall with old newspapers before — a line in the log for June 1965 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Covering the wall with old newspapers on the same day, the operator said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the switch at the far screen, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ cover three miles before the bridge before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Cover three miles before the bridge at once and never mention it again.

By 1978 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the log, and a new trainee from the next station ⑧ covers three miles before the bridge on the same day every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the screen, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ covered the wall with old newspapers again when nobody else would.

⑩ To cover the wall with old newspapers, my mother said in 1983, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody covers the wall with old newspapers before dawn again and somebody must cover the wall with old newspapers on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 覆盖（一般过去式 covered the wall with old newspapers：1971 年操作员头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 覆盖（一般现在 covers the wall with old newspapers：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 覆盖（不定式 to cover the wall with old newspapers：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 覆盖（过去完成时 had covered the wall with old newspapers：1965 年六月的运行日志上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 覆盖（动名词 covering the wall with old newspapers 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 涉及（cover three miles before the bridge：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去涉及过桥之前要走三英里）
G. v. 涉及（cover three miles before the bridge：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 覆盖（后段两处：新来的实习生照例 covers three miles before the bridge，而母亲又一次 covered the wall with old newspapers）

answers.why: cover 意为“覆盖”，1971 年操作员当天就覆盖用旧报纸把墙糊上，那是机房里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 covered。
cover 意为“覆盖”，自那以后操作员天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 covers。
cover 意为“覆盖”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯覆盖用旧报纸把墙糊上”，此处为不定式 to cover the wall with old newspapers。
cover 意为“覆盖”，运行日志里 六月 那行字说明早在 1978 年之前就有人覆盖过，故用过去完成时 had covered。
cover 意为“覆盖”，操作员说“覆盖用旧报纸把墙糊上这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 covering the wall with old newspapers 作主语。
cover 意为“涉及”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去涉及过桥之前要走三英里”，should ever 之后用原形 cover three miles before the bridge。
cover 意为“涉及”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻涉及过桥之前要走三英里（cover three miles before the bridge at once），以后再也不要提起。
cover 意为“覆盖”，新来的实习生每个班次都照例涉及过桥之前要走三英里，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 covers。
cover 意为“覆盖”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就覆盖用旧报纸把墙糊上，用一般过去式 covered 叙述。
cover 意为“覆盖”，结尾那句是母亲 1983 年的话：要覆盖用旧报纸把墙糊上，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和机房记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 cover 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the operator covered the wall with old newspapers on the same day, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the operator covers the wall with old newspapers before dawn whenever the station asks.
Covering the wall with old newspapers on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever cover three miles before the bridge before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new trainee from the next station covers three miles before the bridge on the same day every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother covered the wall with old newspapers again, and the station remembered that half.
